statement: Let bestProfit(w) be defined as follows: if there is at least one i with 0 <= i < len(difficulty) and difficulty[i] <= w, then bestProfit(w) = max{ profit[i] | 0 <= i < len(difficulty) and difficulty[i] <= w }; otherwise bestProfit(w) = 0. The function returns a result r and r = sum_{j=0}^{len(worker)-1} bestProfit(worker[j]).
preconditions: len(difficulty) = len(profit); 1 <= len(difficulty) <= 10000; 1 <= len(worker) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(difficulty), 1 <= difficulty[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= profit[i] <= 100000; and for every j with 0 <= j < len(worker), 1 <= worker[j] <= 100000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r and does not fail: it does not panic, access out of bounds, or overflow i64 arithmetic.
preconditions: len(difficulty) = len(profit); 1 <= len(difficulty) <= 10000; 1 <= len(worker) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(difficulty), 1 <= difficulty[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= profit[i] <= 100000; and for every j with 0 <= j < len(worker), 1 <= worker[j] <= 100000.

statement: Let bestProfit(w) be the maximum profit[i] over all i with 0 <= i < len(difficulty) and difficulty[i] <= w, or 0 if no such i exists. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = len(worker) * bestProfit(w).
preconditions: len(difficulty) = len(profit); 1 <= len(difficulty) <= 10000; 1 <= len(worker) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(difficulty), 1 <= difficulty[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= profit[i] <= 100000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(worker), 1 <= worker[j] <= 100000; and there exists an integer w such that worker[j] = w for every 0 <= j < len(worker).

statement: If the function returns r on (difficulty, profit, worker), r1 on (difficulty, profit, w1), and r2 on (difficulty, profit, w2), then r = r1 + r2.
preconditions: len(difficulty) = len(profit); 1 <= len(difficulty) <= 10000; 1 <= len(worker) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(difficulty), 1 <= difficulty[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= profit[i] <= 100000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(worker), 1 <= worker[j] <= 100000; len(worker) >= 2; w1 and w2 are nonempty slices; len(w1) + len(w2) = len(worker); worker is the concatenation of w1 and w2, meaning worker[j] = w1[j] for 0 <= j < len(w1) and worker[len(w1) + j] = w2[j] for 0 <= j < len(w2); and every element of w1 and w2 is between 1 and 100000.

statement: Let C be the number of j with 0 <= j < len(worker) for which there exists i with 0 <= i < len(difficulty) and difficulty[i] <= worker[j]. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = p * C.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the following hold: (1) there exists a feasible assignment, meaning a choice for each j with 0 <= j < len(worker) of either no job or an index i_j with 0 <= i_j < len(difficulty) and difficulty[i_j] <= worker[j], such that the assignment's total profit, defined as the sum of profit[i_j] over workers assigned a job and 0 for unassigned workers, equals r, and moreover if no job is chosen for j then there is no i with 0 <= i < len(difficulty) and difficulty[i] <= worker[j]; and (2) for every feasible assignment (where a worker may choose no job even if some affordable job exists), its total profit is at most r.
preconditions: len(difficulty) = len(profit); 1 <= len(difficulty) <= 10000; 1 <= len(worker) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(difficulty), 1 <= difficulty[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= profit[i] <= 100000; and for every j with 0 <= j < len(worker), 1 <= worker[j] <= 100000.
